name: sysbio-curie-plugins
description: Six tiny plugins for the Institut Curie MCP hackathon: one skill and five one-feature MCP servers (tools and errors, progress, elicitation, a prompt, a resource) to see the MCP Python SDK v2 syntax once and test how each feature shows up in Claude Code, Codex and VS Code.

claude_marketplace.name: sysbio-curie
claude_marketplace.description: Plugins from the sysbio-curie organisation: the MCP hackathon demo plugins (one skill, five one-feature MCP servers) and, later, real servers for cancer systems biology.

plugins.name: demo-skill
plugins.description: A skill, to see the Agent Skills syntax once: authoring-an-mcp-server, a guide to writing an MCP server with the MCP Python SDK v2.

codex.shortDescription: A skill teaching the MCP Python SDK v2 syntax.
codex.longDescription: Ships one Agent Skill, authoring-an-mcp-server, a guide to writing an MCP server with the MCP Python SDK v2 (tools, resources, prompts, elicitation, progress). No MCP server of its own.
defaultPrompt: Help me write an MCP server for my own analysis.
Which MCP primitive should this be: a tool, a resource or a prompt?

plugins.name: demo-tools
plugins.description: Four arithmetic tools (add, subtract, multiply, divide); divide by zero shows how a tool raises an error the model can read.

codex.shortDescription: Four arithmetic tools and one deliberate tool error.
codex.longDescription: Four arithmetic tools (add, subtract, multiply, divide) implemented with the MCP Python SDK v2. Dividing by zero raises a ToolError instead of crashing, so the model sees a readable failure it can react to.
defaultPrompt: Use demo-tools to divide 10 by 4, then divide 1 by 0.

plugins.name: demo-progress
plugins.description: One slow tool, count_to, that reports progress after each one-second step.

codex.shortDescription: A slow tool that reports progress as it runs.
codex.longDescription: One tool, count_to, that counts from 1 to n with a one-second delay per step and calls the MCP Python SDK v2 progress API after each step, so the host can render a live progress bar.

plugins.name: demo-elicitation
plugins.description: One tool, greet, that asks the user for their name before answering (elicitation via a Resolve resolver).

codex.shortDescription: A tool that asks the user a question before answering.
codex.longDescription: One tool, greet, that elicits the user's name mid-call using the MCP Python SDK v2 Resolve/Elicit pattern (protocol revision 2026-07-28), then greets them by name, showing the accepted/declined/cancelled outcomes.

plugins.name: demo-prompt
plugins.description: No tools; one prompt, summarise_gene, to see how a prompt appears in the host's menu.

codex.shortDescription: One canned prompt, picked by the user, not the model.
codex.longDescription: No tools, one MCP prompt, summarise_gene, that asks for a three-bullet cancer-biology summary of a gene. Prompts are picked by a person from the host's menu (a slash command in Claude Code), never invoked by the model on its own.
defaultPrompt: Run the summarise_gene prompt for TP53.

plugins.name: demo-resource
plugins.description: No tools; one resource (genes://panel) and one resource template (genes://panel/{symbol}).

codex.shortDescription: A gene panel exposed as MCP resources.
codex.longDescription: No tools, one fixed resource (genes://panel, a five-gene oncogene/tumour-suppressor panel as JSON) and one resource template (genes://panel/{symbol}) that the host or model reads by URI rather than calling as a tool.
defaultPrompt: Read the resource genes://panel/KRAS from demo-resource.
